formats.name: Language-gap quiz
formats.description: Contestants translate everyday phrases into Cantonese and fail entertainingly. A*Pop's 'Can These Chinese Americans Pass A Basic Cantonese Language Quiz?' runs multi-million views across rounds.

formats.name: Parent-comparison two-role skit
formats.description: One actor plays both the overbearing Asian parent and the American-raised kid. Steven He's 'How your parents COMPARE you to your cousin' hit ~310K likes.

formats.name: Recurring character
formats.description: A signature persona fans quote back. Jake Sing Chan's 'Ni Howdy' (exaggerated American vs. CNY red-envelope exchange) became a catchphrase engine.

formats.name: 'Phrases Canto moms say' series
formats.description: Serialized listicles of mom-isms. Each entry is a shareable clip and comment bait ('my mom says this too').
formats.example_label: CantotoMando 'Signs you grew up in a Canto Household'

formats.name: 'Cantonese card revoked'
formats.description: Attempt the entire video in Cantonese and fail, with mom roasting off-camera. Relatable incompetence + family comedy.
formats.example_label: Eric Ou 'ABC son gets his Cantonese card revoked'

formats.name: Day-N learning journey
formats.description: Serialized progress vlogs ('Day 152 of practicing Cantonese'). Builds returning viewers; stakes rise with the count.
formats.example_label: Andrew Buoy 'Cantonese & Toisan school for ABCs'

formats.name: Mixed English-Cantonese mum mock
formats.description: Mocking how mums awkwardly force English words into Cantonese sentences ('Jayden, 媽咪 told you 呀, too much 啦'). Went mega-viral in HK; brands trendjacked it.

formats.name: Multilingual persona switch
formats.description: One creator, multiple parenting personas toggled by language. J Lou's sweet-English-mom to scary-Cantonese-mom switch is the template.

ideas.title: Can my husband pass a Cantonese food vocab quiz?
ideas.hook: Have him translate zongzi ingredients and dim sum names on camera. The fails are the content.
ideas.why: Lifts the proven A*Pop quiz format into her husband-wife comedy lane.

ideas.hook: Serialized listicle; each entry a shareable clip. Comment bait: 'my grandma says this too.'
ideas.why: CantotoMando's 'Phrases Canto Moms Say' format, but the Toisan-grandma variant is untapped.

ideas.title: Day N of learning grandma's recipes before they're gone
ideas.hook: Serialized journey with emotional stakes; recipe-preservation content gets saved and shared hard.
ideas.why: Andrew Buoy's journey format with higher emotional stakes.

ideas.title: Rating my grandma's reaction to my cooking
